workstations.checks.C01.title: Protection disabled
workstations.checks.C01.why: A disabled Defender component reduces workstation protection. This does not prove that third-party antivirus is absent.
workstations.checks.C01.action: Review the disabled components and the protection snapshot time.
workstations.checks.C01.remediation: On the workstation, review the Defender policy and restore the required components. Contact the administrator if protection is policy-managed.
workstations.checks.C02.title: New local administrator
workstations.checks.C02.why: Membership in the local Administrators group grants elevated workstation privileges.
workstations.checks.C02.action: Review the added account, the actor and the approval for this change.
workstations.checks.C02.remediation: Review current local Administrators membership and remove unapproved membership using standard administration tools.
workstations.reasons.local_admin_added: An addition to the local Administrators group was recorded.
workstations.reasons.local_admin_removed: Removal from the local Administrators group was recorded.
workstations.reasons.local_admin_baselin: The initial group membership is unknown. Review the event date; the available history does not confirm current membership.
workstations.checks.C03.title: Repeated password failures on a workstation
workstations.checks.C03.why: Frequent sign-in failures may indicate password guessing or a configuration issue. They do not prove an attack.
workstations.checks.C03.action: Compare the target account, source and original sign-in failures.
workstations.checks.C03.remediation: Review saved credentials and service settings at the confirmed source. Restrict unwanted attempts using your established procedure.
workstations.reasons.password_failures: Sign-in failures: at least {count} within {window_minutes} minutes.
workstations.directions.from_station: From the workstation to a server
workstations.checks.C04.title: Suspicious process launch
workstations.checks.C04.why: A launch from a temporary or public directory needs review. The path alone does not prove malicious activity.
workstations.checks.C04.action: Review the path, command line, account and available signature evidence.
workstations.checks.C04.remediation: Inspect the file using the workstation protection tools. Missing signature evidence does not mean the file is unsigned.
workstations.reasons.suspicious_process_: Launch from a directory requiring review: {path}.
workstations.checks.C05.title: New service or scheduled task
workstations.checks.C05.why: A service or scheduled task can keep a program running with elevated privileges.
workstations.checks.C05.action: Review the change type, program and actor, if known.
workstations.checks.C05.remediation: Compare the change with approved maintenance. Correct an unapproved service or task using standard workstation tools.
workstations.reasons.service_or_task_cha: A service or scheduled task change was recorded.
workstations.reasons.task_updated: A scheduled task update was recorded.
workstations.reasons.service_task_baseli: The full list of services and tasks is unknown. Review the event date; the available history does not confirm their current presence. Matching settings do not prove a shared cause.
workstations.checks.C06.title: New removable media
workstations.checks.C06.why: Unfamiliar removable media needs review under your organization’s policy. A connection does not prove that files were copied.
workstations.checks.C06.action: Review the media details and the available history boundary.
workstations.checks.C06.remediation: Compare the media with approved devices. Restrict its use through your standard policy if needed.
workstations.reasons.removable_media_fir: The media was first observed in the available workstation history.
workstations.checks.C07.title: Sign-in outside policy
workstations.checks.C07.why: An interactive sign-in outside the configured working hours may require confirmation.
workstations.checks.C07.action: Review the sign-in method and time, time zone and applied policy version.
workstations.checks.C07.remediation: Confirm why the sign-in was needed. Adjust working hours or access according to the approved policy.
workstations.reasons.logon_outside_polic: Sign-in at {local_time} ({timezone}) outside configured working hours. Policy version: {policy_version}.
workstations.reasons.logon_policy_not_co: Sign-in hours are not configured. Set working days, hours and time zone for the workstation or OU.
workstations.reasons.logon_type_unknown: The sign-in type was not received. Working hours cannot be checked yet.
workstations.logon_policy.title: Workstation sign-in hours
workstations.logon_policy.description: Set working days, hours and time zone for a workstation or OU. Without a policy, working hours are unknown. JSON: version, policies; scope: {kind: station, station_id} or {kind: ou, domain_id, ou_path}; timezone, weekdays (Mon=0), start/end (HH:MM), include_cached_interactive (type 11). Types 2/10 are always checked. A workstation overrides its OU. Increase version when changing the policy. Start is inclusive, end exclusive; overnight shifts use their starting day. Up to 1024 characters.
workstations.logon_policy.validation: Check the JSON, scope, time zone, days and hours. Increase version when changing the policy. Each scope can have only one policy; up to 1024 characters.
workstations.checks.C08.title: Server not reporting
workstations.checks.C08.why: When a server stops reporting, recent events may be unavailable for review.
workstations.checks.C08.action: Distinguish a lost connection from delivery or import delays and a planned pause.
workstations.checks.C08.remediation: Review the agent service, network and delivery status on the server. Address the confirmed cause.
workstations.reasons.server_silent: Server contact has not been confirmed for more than {threshold_seconds} seconds.
workstations.checks.C09.title: Protection data older than one day
workstations.checks.C09.why: An old snapshot does not confirm current protection status. Severity is higher for a server.
workstations.checks.C09.action: Review the last snapshot time and why fresh data is missing.
workstations.checks.C09.remediation: Review Defender state collection and snapshot delivery. After addressing the cause, wait for a new snapshot.
workstations.reasons.protection_stale: The last protection snapshot is more than {age_hours} hours old.
workstations.checks.C10.title: Workstation not reporting
workstations.checks.C10.why: Without workstation contact, recent activity may be missing from the report.
workstations.checks.C10.action: Review workstation availability and agent status, including paused or disabled collection.
workstations.checks.C10.remediation: If the workstation should be online, review its agent service and network. Treat a planned pause separately from a lost connection.
workstations.reasons.workstation_silent: Workstation contact has not been confirmed for more than {threshold_seconds} seconds.
workstations.reasons.source_missing: Some sources are unavailable; their data was not received.
workstations.reasons.coverage_incomplete: Data is incomplete; counts are lower bounds.
workstations.reasons.baseline_unknown: Findings at the previous sign-in are unknown; the new count is unavailable.
workstations.reasons.scope_denied: Access to checks in this scope is denied.
workstations.reasons.data_stale: Data is stale; the current state is unconfirmed.
workstations.reasons.not_collected: Data has not been collected yet.
security.problems.presentation.qw.passwo: These attempts may indicate someone is trying to gain access to your systems.
1) Check whether the user is making mistakes (a password change or an old device). 2) If the source is unfamiliar, block it on the firewall. 3) Change the account password.
Failed sign-ins to {count} accounts from {source} since {time}.
These attempts may indicate someone is trying to gain access to your systems.
1) Block the source on the firewall. 2) Open the list of affected accounts and check for a successful sign-in from the same address.
{account} signed in from {source} at {time} after {count} failed attempts from the same source.
These attempts may indicate someone is trying to gain access to your systems.
1) Change the account password immediately. 2) End its sessions. 3) Check Domain changes for its actions after the sign-in.
security.problems.presentation.spray_thr: Sign-in attempts from {source} against {account_count} accounts · {attempts} attempts
One address produced failed sign-ins for multiple accounts within the rule window.
A successful sign-in from the same address followed failed sign-ins against that account.
security.problems.presentation.spray_wha: One source attempted to sign in to five or more accounts within ten minutes. One or two attempts per account can indicate an automated list attack; regular intervals are supporting evidence.
security.problems.presentation.spray_suc: A successful sign-in followed a password spray
After repeated failures, the same source successfully signed in to an attacked account. An attacker may have gained access.
Check the successful sign-in. If unexpected, isolate the source, end its sessions and reset the password from a trusted computer.
security.problems.presentation.kerberoas: An account requested tickets for many services
{account} requested tickets for {count} services in {minutes} min from {source}.
Source {source} requested RC4 tickets for {count} different service accounts within {seconds} seconds — possible Kerberoasting.
Weak passwords can be recovered from the tickets, granting the services' permissions.
1) Ask the account owner whether they ran a check. 2) If not, change the account password. 3) Change the passwords of the service accounts in the list; set long passwords for them.
security.problems.presentation.asrep_tit: Ticket requested for an account without pre-authentication
security.problems.presentation.asrep_wha: A ticket for {account} was issued without pre-authentication, requested from {source} at {time}.
security.problems.presentation.asrep_obs: Source {source} obtained a ticket for account {account} without pre-authentication — possible AS-REP roasting.
security.problems.presentation.asrep_why: The password can be guessed offline without further failed sign-ins or account lockouts.
security.problems.presentation.asrep_nex: 1) Clear the account option "Do not require Kerberos preauthentication". 2) Change its password.
security.problems.presentation.preauth_t: Kerberos pre-authentication is disabled on an account
security.problems.presentation.preauth_w: The AD snapshot shows a user with DONT_REQ_PREAUTH enabled. This is an unsafe setting, not proof of an attack.
Knowing the account name is enough to obtain material for offline password guessing.
security.problems.presentation.preauth_n: Clear 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' in account properties. Check application compatibility and refresh the AD snapshot.
security.problems.presentation.fanout_ti: One account rapidly signed in to several computers
security.problems.presentation.fanout_wh: One account successfully signed in through the network or RDP to several computers in a short period — possible lateral movement.
security.problems.presentation.fanout_ob: Account {account} successfully signed in through the network or RDP to {count} different computers within {seconds} seconds — possible lateral movement.
security.problems.presentation.fanout_wh: A stolen account may be used to rapidly access other computers.
security.problems.presentation.fanout_ne: Ask the account owner whether these sign-ins were planned. If unexpected, end the sessions, isolate affected computers and reset the password. Add known service accounts to policy exclusions.
security.problems.presentation.privilege: An account was added to an administrators group
An account was created and added to a privileged group within ten minutes — possible attacker persistence.
The new permissions can allow control over the domain, accounts or backups.
1) Ask {actor} whether this was planned. 2) If not, remove {member} from the group and reset the password of {actor}.
1) Check who changed the group's membership and whether it was planned. 2) If it was unplanned, remove the added account and reset the password of whoever added it.
security.problems.presentation.identity_: This behaviour requires review and does not prove AI involvement. Audit coverage depends on the available sources.
security.problems.presentation.brute_tit: Repeated password attempts against one account
security.problems.presentation.brute_thr: Failed sign-ins against one account reached the rule threshold.
A successful sign-in followed repeated failed sign-ins against the same account.
security.problems.presentation.brute_wha: At least ten bad-password failures affected one account within five minutes.
security.problems.presentation.disabled_: Sign-in attempted with a disabled account
Windows rejected a sign-in because the account was disabled.
security.problems.presentation.password_: These attempts may indicate someone is trying to gain access to your systems.
Check the linked attempts. If they were unexpected, block the source and secure the affected accounts.
Failed attempts do not prove that access was gained.
security.problems.presentation.watch_tit: Activity of an account under watch
security.problems.presentation.watch_wha: Native evidence identifies an account under watch at event time. Activities are grouped by account, source and event family in five-minute episodes.
security.problems.presentation.watch_why: Account watch raises severity by one level, capped at critical. It does not increase confidence.
security.problems.presentation.watch_nex: Review the linked events and the account watch entry.
security.problems.presentation.watch_lim: Watch is priority context. This activity alone does not prove compromise or complete audit coverage.
watch.denied: Access to account watch in this scope is denied.
watch.conflict: The entry changed. Refresh the list and try again.
watch.failed: Could not save account watch. Check the account, reason and future expiry.
security.problems.presentation.file_deco: File audit recorded a touch of a file labelled as a decoy at event time. Touch details show its exact meaning and outcome.
Any observed decoy touch, including denied access, requires investigation.
Review the evidence and the selected label version in the decoy registry, and check audit readiness.
An access check does not prove a data read. A specific observation is confirmed; complete audit coverage and the absence of other touches are not proven.

security.problems.presentation.privilege: Account added to an administrators group
An account was added to a privileged domain group (for example, Domain Admins).
This is how attackers take hold of a network: a member of this group can do anything in the domain. If nobody planned it, it may be an attack.
Find out who added the account and why. If nobody planned it, remove it from the group right away and reset the passwords of that account and of whoever added it.
security.problems.presentation.dc_schedu: New scheduled task on a domain controller
Windows recorded a new scheduled task named {target}.
Windows recorded a new scheduled task.
security.problems.presentation.dc_servic: New service on a domain controller
Windows recorded the installation of the service {target}.
Windows recorded a new service installation.
security.problems.presentation.scheduled: Scheduled task created on a computer
A new task was registered in Windows Task Scheduler.
Malware and intruders often use scheduled tasks to start their program again after a reboot.
Open the task on the computer and check which program it runs. If nobody created it, disable it and scan the computer with antivirus.
security.problems.presentation.eventlog_: Someone cleared the Windows security log.
Intruders clear the log to hide their tracks. Normal work almost never requires it.
Find out who cleared the log. If it was not a planned admin action, treat the computer as compromised: disconnect it from the network and reset passwords of accounts used on it.
security.problems.presentation.decoy_wha: Authentication evidence exactly identifies an account labelled as a decoy at event time.
security.problems.presentation.decoy_why: Any attempt to use a decoy, including a failed sign-in, requires investigation.
security.problems.presentation.decoy_nex: Review the native event, the attempt source and the decoy label version active at event time.
security.problems.presentation.decoy_lim: This event proves a specific use. It does not establish complete audit coverage or the absence of other attempts.
security.problems.presentation.audit_why: Audit policy change can disable or alter security event logging and requires validity check.
security.problems.presentation.audit_nex: Check related events, confirm initiator, and match change against approved audit baseline. If not approved, escalate to investigation.
security.problems.presentation.default_n: Open evidence and perform manual check.
security.problems.presentation.audit_lim: Custom description for this policy is not registered.

reports.v2.security.problems.description: Published results of accepted checks: what happened, why it matters, evidence and the analyst's decision.
security.problems.presentation.wording_l: Custom description for this rule is not registered.
reports.v2.security.problems.limitations: A zero queue does not mean there are no problems: analysis freshness is not confirmed.
reports.v2.security.problems.intent.ques: Which published problems need an analyst decision in the selected scope?
reports.v2.security.problems.intent.deno: Applicable accepted rules × authorized subjects × processing windows; finding count is not the denominator.
reports.v2.security.problems.intent.fres: Check result publication time is shown separately from source event time and data loading time.
reports.ad.checks.column.title: Check
reports.ad.checks.users.disabled_logon.w: A successful logon after an observed disable event needs investigation; a snapshot alone does not prove a bypass.
reports.ad.checks.users.disabled_logon.a: Check the logon source and account state on domain controllers.
reports.ad.checks.users.disabled_logon.r: Correlate 4725, subsequent 4722 and 4624 by SID; check replication and existing sessions.
reports.ad.checks.users.new_privileged.w: A new direct or nested administrative group member gains sensitive privileges.
reports.ad.checks.users.new_privileged.a: Confirm authorization and the owner of the change.
reports.ad.checks.users.new_privileged.r: Review the standard administrative group chain and request; revoke unauthorized membership.
reports.ad.checks.users.reversible_passw: Allowing reversible storage increases password disclosure risk.
Review whether the setting is required.
Disable Store password using reversible encryption and arrange a password change.
reports.ad.checks.users.inactive_privile: An unused privileged account retains sensitive membership.
Review the purpose and need for privileges.
Review direct and nested membership; remove unnecessary privileges with owner approval.
reports.ad.checks.users.spn_privileged.w: An SPN on a privileged account increases the impact of service password compromise.
reports.ad.checks.users.spn_privileged.r: Review SPN purpose; remove unnecessary privileges or migrate the service to gMSA.

security.problems.presentation.t109.rans: Host {host}. A host ran a command to destroy backups, disable recovery or stop backup services.
Ransomware often destroys recovery options before encrypting files.
Immediately check the host and command initiator. If unauthorized, isolate the host, restrict the account and protect offline backups.
A command or script was observed; successful backup deletion and encryption are not proven.
security.problems.presentation.t109.secu: {actor} cleared the security log on {computer} at {time}.
Clearing the log can hide an attack and interrupt SLI observation.
1) Ask {actor} why this was done. 2) If nobody confirms it, treat the computer as compromised: reset administrator passwords and review “Domain changes” for the day before the log was cleared.
1) Ask the administrators why the log was cleared. 2) If nobody confirms it, reset administrator passwords and review Domain changes for the day before the log was cleared.
The log clear is confirmed; the initiator intent needs investigation.
security.problems.presentation.t109.audi: Auditing was turned off on a computer
{actor} turned off auditing of {category} on {computer} at {time}.
An attacker may disable auditing before theft or encryption.
1) Restore the setting: in SLI, “Agents” → computer → “Audit”. 2) Ask {actor} why it was changed.
Restore the audit setting in the computer's details on the Agents page.
The audit change is confirmed; approved maintenance may also cause it.
security.problems.presentation.t109.agen: The SLI agent was stopped or disabled
The agent service on {computer} was stopped at {time}; startup changed by {actor}.
Loss of observation may precede a fast attack.
1) Start the `SLIAgentNet` service on the computer. 2) If you did not stop it, check Domain changes for {actor}.
1) Start the SLIAgentNet service on the computer. 2) If the stop was unplanned, review Domain changes.
A deletion command proves an attempt. Event 7045 proves disabled installation, not service deletion.
SLI delivery stopped after a dangerous event
Host {host}. Event delivery is overdue despite recent authenticated contact, following log clearing, audit removal or ransomware preparation.
Observation was lost during a suspicious sequence.
Urgently inspect the host through an independent channel, its services and logs. Protect backups and isolate the host if an attack is confirmed.
Recent agent contact does not establish overall host health. Ordinary C08/C10 silence does not create this signal.
security.problems.presentation.t109.file: Host {host}. Confirmed writes or deletions crossed the fast policy threshold: by default 30 distinct files in 30 seconds.
Machine-speed changes require investigation before encryption spreads.
Check the account, process and files. For unauthorized changes, isolate the source and temporarily restrict share writes.
Encryption is not proven. The existing 100 files in 300 seconds threshold continues separately.
security.problems.presentation.t109.mass: Mass file reads or read access checks
Host {host}. One account crossed the policy threshold: by default 200 distinct files or 10 distinct shares in 5 minutes.
Mass access may precede data theft and extortion.
Check the account, access source and approved exports. Restrict suspicious accounts and investigate outbound transfers; exclude approved backup accounts through policy.
4663 records access; 5145 records a read access check. Transferred volume and exfiltration are not proven.

security.problems.ad_hardening.view_note: Recommendations from a saved snapshot: what to fix before an attack. Domain, severity and search within displayed objects apply. These are configuration checks, not evidence of an attack.
security.problems.ad_hardening.list_trun: Total objects: {count}; only the first part of the list is shown.
security.problems.ad_hardening.limitatio: Only saved AD configuration is checked. No problems does not mean a safe domain: unknown fields are not assessed. LAPS metadata and logon times require review; passwords are never read. An administrator applies changes separately.
security.problems.ad_hardening.partial: A snapshot is missing, bounded or incomplete. Lists and counts cover available objects, not the entire domain.
security.problems.ad_hardening.stale: The snapshot is older than 48 hours or dated in the future. Refresh it before changing configuration.
security.problems.ad_hardening.spn_users: Accounts with service names (SPNs): {count}. These usually run SQL, 1C or IIS services; a long password is essential.
These are usually SQL, 1C or IIS service accounts; a short password can be guessed from a service ticket (Kerberos).
Set a long random service account password together with the service owner.
security.problems.ad_hardening.rc4.title: Accounts with weak Kerberos encryption risk
security.problems.ad_hardening.rc4.what: User accounts with SPNs, RC4 enabled and no AES: {count}. Empty attributes and computers are not assessed.
security.problems.ad_hardening.rc4.why: Weak service ticket encryption makes password guessing easier (RC4).
security.problems.ad_hardening.rc4.actio: Check whether the service supports AES encryption before disabling RC4.
security.problems.ad_hardening.unconstra: TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION is set on users or non-DC computers: {count}.
A compromised service may act as an administrator who signed in (delegation).
Check with the service owner whether unconstrained delegation is required.
security.problems.ad_hardening.constrain: Accounts with constrained delegation to sensitive service classes: {count}. This is information for review, not a confirmed vulnerability.
A compromised service may access the files or databases it is allowed to use (delegation).
Review the permitted delegation targets with the service owner (msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo).
security.problems.ad_hardening.laps.what: Non-DC computers with no LAPS schema or no returned rotation metadata: {count}. Unavailable metadata does not prove LAPS is absent.
security.problems.ad_hardening.laps.why: A shared local administrator password makes it easier to access several computers.
security.problems.ad_hardening.laps.acti: Check that the local administrator password rotation policy is applied (Windows LAPS).
security.problems.ad_hardening.old_servi: Service account passwords have not been rotated
Accounts with SPNs and passwords older than {threshold} days: {count}. Managed MSA/gMSA accounts are excluded.
An unchanged password leaves more time for guessing or exploiting a leak.
Arrange password rotation with the service owner.
security.problems.ad_hardening.privilege: Enabled privileged accounts with the password-never-expires flag: {count}.
A stolen administrator password may remain usable for a long time.
Review the password rotation schedule with the account owner.
security.problems.ad_hardening.machine_a: MachineAccountQuota is above zero in {count} domains.
Domain users can create computer accounts using the domain quota.
Set MachineAccountQuota to zero if computer enrollment is delegated separately.
security.problems.ad_hardening.lockout_t: Password policies without a lockout threshold: {count}.
Repeated password attempts do not trigger account lockout under these policies.
Set an account lockout threshold in the affected policies.
security.problems.ad_hardening.admin_gro: Administrative groups have too many members
Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins or Administrators groups with more than {threshold} unique members: {count}. Nested groups are expanded and each member is counted once.
Every unnecessary administrator account increases the risk of losing control of the domain.
Review why each administrator group member needs access.
security.problems.ad_hardening.inactive_: Enabled privileged accounts whose latest available logon is older than {threshold} days: {count}. Accounts without a timestamp are not assessed.
A forgotten administrator account is easier to use unnoticed.
Confirm with the account owner that administrative access is still needed.
